text:
B: Hiya! There we go. Can you hear me?
A: Loud and clear. Ryan, Stockport. You're Kerry, yeah? I said in the photo bit you look exactly like my sister. The calendar, the kettle, all of it.
B: *(laughs)* Is that a good thing?
A: It's a great thing. She's a machine, she organises everyone. I live in her spare room at the minute, so I'm biased.
B: Oh, she sounds like my kind of woman. Taunton, by the way. Somerset.
A: Somerset! Cider. That's all I know about Somerset, mate. Cider and Glastonbury.
B: That's about right, to be fair. What do you do, then?
A: I run a bar and music venue, Northern Quarter in Manchester. Eighteen staff, booking, licensing. And you're the NHS, I'm guessing? You've got the shifts on the calendar.
B: Radiographer. X-ray, some CT. And yes, that calendar runs my life.
A: See, I'd be useless at that. I just turn up. My rotas get done, but they get done at the last minute, do you know what I mean.
B: Oh, that would drive me mad. Proper mad. I do the students' rotas at work and if someone sends me a swap the night before, I'm, no. Sorry. No.
A: *(laughs)* You'd sack me.
B: I wouldn't sack you, I'd just give you a checklist. Several checklists.
A: I'd lose them.
B: I'd laminate them.
A: Ha! Okay, you win. What do you do for fun, then, when you're not laminating?
B: Netball on a Tuesday, goal defence. Parkrun on a Saturday. Mostly for the coffee after, but I got a PB last week. Eight seconds.
A: Eight seconds is eight seconds. I've got into padel. Have you played padel? It's like tennis but—
B: In a cage, yeah, my husband's mates keep going on about it.
A: It's brilliant, though! Honestly, you'd love it, you're competitive, I can tell. Goal defence, that's a competitive position, that.
B: *(laughs)* Fair. I'm fairly loud watching the rugby as well. Bath, mostly. Darren just sits there and I'm up off the sofa.
A: I'm the same at County. I'm the one shouting at the ref. Here, what do you do for food down there? I'm always looking for places.
B: Oh, I'm not the one to ask. Same curry house every Friday, same order. Chicken tikka masala and a peshwari naan, it's lush, why change it?
A: Nah, Kerry, you've got to branch out. There's a Vietnamese place round the corner from work, I've told everyone today about it, I'm like a stuck record.
B: You can tell me, I'm still having the tikka masala.
A: *(laughs)* Same with holidays, I bet. Same place every year?
B: Bude every summer, camping with friends. Spain in the autumn, somewhere we've been before. Sun, a pool and someone else cooking. That's a holiday.
A: I went to Mexico City on my own last year. Didn't book a thing. Just turned up, found the bar where the locals go.
B: See, that's my nightmare. Is that what you're after, someone to tell you you're brave?
A: *(laughs)* Bit, yeah. Bit—
